# FMAP Time Series Analysis

## 1. Data Import and Preparation

```{r}


# Load packages
library(fpp3)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Import dataset
fmap <- read_csv("FMAP_Marina.csv")

# Inspect data
glimpse(fmap)
summary(fmap)


```

```{r}

# Create monthly tsibble
fmap_ts <- fmap |>
  mutate(Date = yearmonth(Date)) |>
  as_tsibble(
    key = c(EFPG_name, Metroregion_name),
    index = Date
  )

# Inspect tsibble
fmap_ts

# Check missing observations
count_gaps(fmap_ts)


# Check missing values across the entire dataset
fmap_ts |>
  as_tibble() |>
  summarise(
    total_observations = n(),
    missing_prices = sum(is.na(Price_index_GEKS))
  )


# Check for duplicate keys
duplicates <- fmap |>
  count(EFPG_name, Metroregion_name, Date) |>
  filter(n > 1)

duplicates

# Check number of observations per subseries
fmap_ts |>
  count(EFPG_name, Metroregion_name)

```

## 2. Exploratory Data Analysis

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8
#| dpi: 150

# Shorten region labels for plotting
fmap_plot <- fmap_ts |>
  mutate(
    Region = sub("Census Region [1-4]: ", "",
                 Metroregion_name)
  )

# Plot first five food categories
fmap_plot |>
  filter(EFPG_name %in% sort(unique(EFPG_name))[1:5]) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = Date,
    y = Price_index_GEKS,
    color = Region
  )) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.65) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ EFPG_name,
    ncol = 2,
    labeller = label_wrap_gen(28)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Food Price Indexes, 2012–2018",
    subtitle = "First five assigned food categories",
    x = "Year",
    y = "GEKS Price Index",
    color = "Region"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
```

```{r}

# Compare regions for one food category
```

## 3. Training and Testing Split

```{r}

# Split into training and testing sets
train <- fmap_ts |>
  filter(year(Date) <= 2017)

test <- fmap_ts |>
  filter(year(Date) == 2018)

# Verify observations
train |>
  count(EFPG_name, Metroregion_name)

test |>
  count(EFPG_name, Metroregion_name)

```

## 4. Seasonal Strength Analysis

```{r}
# Calculate seasonal strength 
#| label: seasonal-strength
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Calculate seasonal strength using training data
seasonal_strength <- train |>
  features(Price_index_GEKS, feat_stl)

# Display seasonal strength results
seasonal_strength |>
  select(
    EFPG_name,
    Metroregion_name,
    seasonal_strength_year
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(seasonal_strength_year)) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

```{r}
# Visualize seasonal strength 
#| label: seasonal-strength-heatmap
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
#| dpi: 150
#| message: false
#| warning: false

seasonal_strength |>
  mutate(
    Region = sub(
      "Census Region [1-4]: ",
      "",
      Metroregion_name
    ),
    Category = stringr::str_wrap(EFPG_name, 35)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = Region,
    y = Category,
    fill = seasonal_strength_year
  )) +
  geom_tile(
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", seasonal_strength_year)),
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "white",
    high = "steelblue4",
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Seasonal Strength by Food Category and Region",
    subtitle = "STL decomposition of monthly GEKS price indexes, 2012–2017",
    x = "Region",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Seasonal\nStrength"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )



```

```{r}
#| label: seasonal-strength-summary
#| message: false
#| warning: false

seasonal_strength |>
  group_by(EFPG_name) |>
  summarise(
    mean_seasonal_strength = mean(
      seasonal_strength_year,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    min_seasonal_strength = min(
      seasonal_strength_year,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    max_seasonal_strength = max(
      seasonal_strength_year,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_seasonal_strength)) |>
  print(n = Inf)


```

```{r}
# Export seasonal strength results 
#| label: export-seasonal-strength
#| message: false
#| warning: false

seasonal_strength |>
  select(
    EFPG_name,
    Metroregion_name,
    seasonal_strength_year
  ) |>
  rename(
    category = EFPG_name,
    region = Metroregion_name,
    seasonal_strength = seasonal_strength_year
  ) |>
  write_csv("FMAP_Marina_Seasonality.csv")
```

## 

## 5. Forecasting Models

### 5.1 Fit SNAIVE, ETS, and ARIMA Models

```{r}
# Fit forecasting models
fits <- train |>
  model(
    SNAIVE = SNAIVE(Price_index_GEKS),
    ETS = ETS(Price_index_GEKS),
    ARIMA = ARIMA(Price_index_GEKS)
  )

# Display fitted models
fits

```

### 5.2 Forecast 2018

```{r}

# Generate 12-month forecasts
forecasts <- fits |>
  forecast(h = "12 months")

# Inspect forecasts
forecasts

```

### 5.3 Visualize Forecasts

```{r}

# Plot forecasts for one subseries
forecasts |>
  filter(
    EFPG_name == "Baked goods",
    Metroregion_name == "Census Region 4: West"
  ) |>
  autoplot(
    fmap_ts |>
      filter(
        EFPG_name == "Baked goods",
        Metroregion_name == "Census Region 4: West",
        year(Date) >= 2016
      ),
    level = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Baked Goods in Western Region: 2018 Forecast Comparison",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Price Index"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

## 6. Model Evaluation

```{r}

# Evaluate forecasts against 2018 actual values
accuracy_results <- forecasts |>
  accuracy(
    test,
    measures = list(
      RMSE = RMSE,
      MAE = MAE,
      MAPE = MAPE
    )
  )

# View accuracy results
accuracy_results

```

### Export Results

```{r}

accuracy_export <- accuracy_results |>
  transmute(
    category = EFPG_name,
    region = Metroregion_name,
    model = .model,
    RMSE,
    MAE,
    MAPE
  )

# Inspect results
print(accuracy_export, n = 20)

# Export CSV
write_csv(
  accuracy_export,
  "FMAP_Marina_Accuracy.csv"
)

```

### Compare Average Model Performance

```{r}

accuracy_export |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(
    mean_RMSE = mean(RMSE, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_MAE = mean(MAE, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_MAPE = mean(MAPE, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(mean_RMSE)

```

```{r}

best_models <- accuracy_export |>
  group_by(category, region) |>
  slice_min(RMSE, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()

# Count how often each model performs best
best_models |>
  count(model, name = "number_of_wins")

# View the best model for each subseries
best_models

```

```{r}

accuracy_export |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(
    mean_RMSE = mean(RMSE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = reorder(model, mean_RMSE),
    y = mean_RMSE
  )) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue4", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.4f", mean_RMSE)),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 4
  ) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(0, 0.022)) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Forecast Error by Model",
    subtitle = "2018 test period across 40 subseries",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean RMSE (index units)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )

```

```{r}

accuracy_export |>
  group_by(category, model) |>
  summarise(
    mean_RMSE = mean(RMSE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(category, mean_RMSE) |>
  print(n = Inf)

```
